etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin cancer (“crab”), a calque of Ancient Greek καρκίνος (karkínos, “crab; ulcer; cancer”) (possibly cognate), applied to cancerous tumors because the enlarged veins resembled the legs of a crab. Doublet of canker and chancre.

definitions.definition: (medicine, oncology, pathology) A disease in which the cells of a tissue undergo uncontrolled (and often rapid) proliferation.

quote.citation: 2006, Edwin Black, chapter 1, in Internal Combustion‎[1]:
quote.text: If successful, Edison and Ford—in 1914—would move society away from the […] hazards of gasoline cars: air and water pollution, noise and noxiousness, constant coughing and the undeniable rise in cancers caused by smoke exhaust particulates.

quote.citation: 2013 June 22, “Snakes and ladders”, in The Economist, volume 407, number 8841, page 76:
quote.text: Risk is everywhere. From tabloid headlines insisting that coffee causes cancer (yesterday, of course, it cured it) to stern government warnings about alcohol and driving, the world is teeming with goblins. For each one there is a frighteningly precise measurement of just how likely it is to jump from the shadows and get you.

quote.citation: 2015 February 26, Francis S. Collins, Harold Varmus, “A New Initiative on Precision Medicine”, in The New England Journal of Medicine, volume 372, number 9, →DOI, pages 793–794:
quote.text: Cancers are common diseases; in the aggregate, they are among the leading causes of death nationally and worldwide, and their incidence is increasing as the population ages.

definitions.definition: (figuratively) Something damaging that spreads throughout something else.

quote.citation: 1991, Charlie Peacock (lyrics and music), “In the Light”‎[2]:
quote.text: The disease of the self runs through my blood; It's a cancer fatal to my soul.

quote.citation: 1999, Bruce Clifford Ross-Larson, Effective Writing‎[3], page 134:
quote.text: Sierra Leone's post-dictator problems are almost absurd in their breadth. It once exported rice; now it can't feed itself. The life span of the average citizen is 39, the shortest in Africa. Unemployment stands at 87 percent and tuberculosis is spreading out of control. Corruption, brazen and ubiquitous, is a cancer on the economy.
